text:
logan: Heads up — since the prebind heartbeat change rolled out to us-west1, I'm seeing a bump in tiny-gang evictions and a trickle of pods falling back to smaller slots. Not huge but correlated with the rollout window. anyone else?

jamie: saw that too, esp in us-west1a. latency on attach/heartbeat goes from ~120ms to 300-400ms for a subset of warmnodes. pods start preempting then requeue, leads to churn.

priya: do we have traces tying the heartbeat to the scheduler's lease refresh path? Could be a conntrack/egress saturation causing attach delays.

logan: i grabbed scheduler logs and a snippet shows repeated prebind timeout for same lease IDs. excerpt: ```scheduler: prebind failed for pod gpu-train-xyz lease: L-12345 timeout=10s attaching to node=n1-usw1a warmnode attach_err=timeout```

drew: interesting — metrics show a small spike in egress from the warm-pool mesh around the same time. Also NVLink health looked fine. suspecting either transient NAT port exhaustion on the warmnode side or an attach RPC throttle at the attach service.

priya: can we check node conntrack/syn backlog? iirc last time something similar was conntrack + calico iptables rules interacting.

logan: checked one host: conntrack entries ~ 85k (limit 100k) and ephemeral port reuse high. Also saw a couple of kubelet warnings: `attach-detach timeout: rpc failed: context deadline exceeded`

jamie: are these tiny-gang jobs more likely to get preempted because of fractional GPU spread? they request fractional gpus and prebind tries to find co-located slots. If attach is slow, scheduler gives up and moves on -> more fragmentation.

drew: yes, the scheduling path has a 10s attach deadline currently. If attach latency > deadline we fall back. For fractional packs that fall back we often leave behind stranded allocations and tiny holes -> aggregating fragmentation.

priya: bumping attach deadline might reduce churn but increases tail latency for the requesting job. maybe better to throttle rollout: revert prebind heartbeat change for a single AZ and observe?

logan: rolling rollback to us-west1a now (canary). also adding temporary alert on attach latency > 150ms to catch early.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started for prebind-heartbeat in us-west1a by logan. ETA ~4m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jamie: while rollback runs, ops question — do we have a cheap mitigation to reduce fragmentation? maybe a short coalescer job that consolidates tiny holes every 5m?

drew: we do have the shelf-coalescer but it's disabled in us-west1 to avoid double-repacks. we could enable it for just the canary AZ for 30m window. low risk.

priya: fine with that. also can we patch scheduler to prefer `attach_pending` nodes last for fractional packs so we don't perpetually bounce? i can open a short PR to add an attach-backoff scoring tweak.

logan: plz do. i'll monitor evictions and costs. current estimate: extra churn added ~2k token-hours on GPUs this morning (~$1.3k) due to repeated restarts and failed warmnode attaches. want to avoid that repeating.

jamie: thanks. if rollback heals, we should run a tight postmortem: root cause (heartbeat amplification -> egress saturation or conntrack) and a small runbook to toggle attach deadline/enable coalescer.

drew: logged an incident page. i'll collect kernel conntrack snapshots + attach service traces and post here when ready.

logan: perfect. tagging @oncall for visibility. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
